**Company**: Salesforce

**Process**: OA + Technical Round + In-person Drive

The initial technical round was 60 minutes and consisted of DSA
**Coding Question 1 — Minimum Window**
Given a string consisting of n words and an array of k required words, return the minimum contiguous sequence of words containing all the required words.
The matching condition was all-or-none:
	• If all required words are present → return the minimum window.
	• If even one required word is missing → return an empty string.
This required identifying a sliding-window pattern.

**Coding Question 2 — Permutations**
Given a word containing unique characters, return a list containing all possible permutations of those characters.
This was a straightforward backtracking problem.

	1. DSA
	2. Design
	3. Hiring Manager

**DSA Question 1 — Ball Collision
Given a sequence of incoming balls, where each ball has:
	• direction: +1 or -1
	• strength
Two balls collide when:
one is moving right (+1)
and
the other is moving left (-1)
When they collide:
	• the ball with greater strength survives
	• if both have the same strength, both are destroyed
Return the indexes of the balls that remain after all possible collisions.
This was essentially a stack/simulation problem, but the problem was presented as a real-world scenario rather than explicitly identifying the pattern.

	• If the next peak is lower or equal, there is no climbing cost.
	• A helicopter can be used subject to a given limit and can cover an arbitrary height difference.
The objective was to determine the furthest peak reachable under the available resources.
This was an optimization/resource-allocation problem

Infosys DSE role interview experience
I appeared for the Infosys DSE role interview on 9th May 2026. Sharing my experience here in case it helps someone.

First, all the candidates selected for the DSE role were asked to sit in a room. Around 10 candidates were taken at a time, and everyone was seated with enough distance between each other to avoid cheating.

We were then given 2 coding questions and around 15 minutes to solve them on pen and paper. The interviewer specifically mentioned that he was looking for the most optimal approach.

Questions asked:

1. Move all the zeros in an array to one end. (He did not specify left or right.)
2. Find the second maximum element in an array.

After that, the sheets were collected in the order in which candidates submitted them, and interviews started one by one. Each interview lasted around 10 minutes maximum.

In my interview, the interviewer directly asked me to explain the code I had written instead of asking for an introduction. After I explained both solutions, he went through my resume.

Since I had mentioned React in my resume, he asked:

* Do you know React?
* How would you optimize the performance of a website?

I had also mentioned Google OAuth, so he asked some surface-level questions about OAuth 2.0. In general, whatever technologies or keywords I had written on my resume (OAuth, bcrypt, etc.), he asked basic conceptual questions related to them, usually with at most one follow-up question.

There were also a few Object-Oriented Programming questions:

* How do you instantiate a class?
* Questions on compile-time and runtime polymorphism.

He also asked a few JavaScript questions, though I do not remember them clearly now.

There was no HR round for the DSE role, only this single technical round. After all the interviews were completed, we were asked to leave, and they informed us that the results would be communicated later.

Overall, the interview felt more resume-based and fundamentals-oriented rather than deep DSA-heavy.

Hope this helps. All the best to everyone preparing!
